silhouette.reason: Mohawk, tusks and heavy shoulders read as an orc; the head sits upright, not hunched.
fixes: push the trapezius higher and the head forward (hunched stance)

proportions.reason: A heavier brow shelf and a flatter, wider nose now read as an orc face rather than a tinted human.
fixes: lower the eyes under the brow shelf and widen the jaw

materials.reason: The mohawk now has loose tips and reads as hair in SIDE; the skin has sheen but it is uniform over head and shoulders, so it reads as plastic.
fixes: vary roughness: rougher on scalp and shoulders, sheen on nose and brow
pores or mottling in the green skin

detail.reason: Tusks, teeth, scar and crest; no skin wrinkles or pores.
fixes: LOD0 wrinkle/pore displacement and a gum strip

wear.reason: A clear cheek scar and blotchy skin tell some history.
fixes: chipped tusk tip and a second scar

lod.reason: FAR LOD2 is still a distance-field re-mesh: the face breaks into flat patches of different tone and the features smear.
fixes: LOD2 from an authored coarse topology (decimated quad base mesh) instead of the distance-field re-mesh, keeping vertex colour smooth
